title: Artifacts: media model, custody and serving
heading: Artifacts: small, exact, permanent
text: A Drops artifact is a media object small enough to sit inside its own proof. There is no separate content server to trust, no envelope to reassemble, and no chunking convention to get wrong. What the leaf holds is what the artifact is.

title: Artifacts: media model, custody and serving
heading: The 256-byte decision

title: Artifacts: media model, custody and serving
heading: No reassembly

text: Drops does not invent a transaction format. It reuses the Taproot script path exactly as BIP 341 defines it, and adds one rule: the leaf you reveal must be a Drops leaf, and it must be the leaf the output actually committed to.
